doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Hearing Joe Williams with Basie
summary: Gates identifies Joe Williams, the first gentleman blues singer he heard with the Basie band.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: That’s Mr. Williams. Big Joe Williams.

We had a great relationship with him actually. He helped us get this project started. He had a relationship with Hamilton College and he got an honorary degree there, so I got to be in his presence on occasion. Those guys had an aura, some of them.
And I don’t know where it came from.

Yeah. There’s a glow. I don’t know where it comes from either but yeah, I sure do recognize it in some people. He was one of the first people that I heard with big bands, because my father played Count Basie. So I heard Joe Williams with Count Basie. And he’s got a very distinctive sound. Maybe I read this somewhere but he was like the first gentleman blues singer. You know, articulate. His notes were right on. He didn’t — I mean I don’t know what Mr. Williams did but he never sounded like he was drunk. A lot of blues singers sounded like [slurs words] but he was articulate and enunciation was right on. But he sang some sure enough blues.
